newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Italian graftbusters seek slush funds in HK - paper.
newsitem.headline: Italian graftbusters seek slush funds in HK - paper.

text.p: Italian graftbusters are trying to trace an estimated US$60 million believed hidden in Hong Kong by corrupt Italian politicians -- fearing it may be inaccessible after the British colony's handover to China, a newspaper reported on Sunday.

An earlier attempt by Rome to claim the cash led to accusations that the territory was protecting slush funds, the South China Morning Post said, quoting Alberto Bradanini, Italy's Consul-General in Hong Kong.

The newspaper said the slush fund allegedly is connected to a corruption scandal involving former Italian prime minister Bettino Craxi, who went into exile in Tunisia to avoid a prison sentence for bribery.
Craxi has denied hiding money in Hong Kong, the daily said.

Italian investigators believe up to US$60 million in bribes for public works contracts and illegal activities is sitting in an account with the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd., the newspaper said.
Prosecutors were finalising a request from the president of the Court of Milan for information about the account, it said.
A similar request earlier by anti-corruption crusader Judge Antonio Di Pietro failed in 1995, the newspaper said.
The Hong Kong courts blocked the request because it came from a prosecutor and not a Milan court, a requirement under the British Common Law system in the territory, it said.
Other funds from the scandal had been hidden in the Cayman Islands, Jersey and Singapore, the newspaper said.
Neither Bradanini nor HSBC officials were immediately available for comment.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese control on July 1 after more than 150 years as a British colony.
